official_syllabus_verbatim: Kant: Possibility of Synthetic a priori Judgments; Space and Time; Categories; Ideas of Reason; Antinomies; Critique of Proofs for the Existence of God.

core_sessions.title: The Critical Project: From Rationalist Dogma and Humean Scepticism to Critique
core_sessions.plain: Kant asks how necessary knowledge can be informative without claiming access to reality beyond experience.
core_sessions.technical: Critical philosophy is transcendental inquiry into the a priori conditions that make possible experience and objective knowledge possible; it accepts sensory content from empiricism, a priori form from rationalism, and limits theoretical cognition to phenomena.
core_sessions.answer: Kant reconciles rationalism and empiricism by making a priori form the condition of experiential objectivity while denying that pure reason can convert those forms into knowledge of noumena.
core_sessions.usage: Begin with the rationalist claim to necessity and Hume's denial that experience yields necessity; then state Kant's transcendental solution and its phenomenal limit.
core_sessions.mechanism: Sensory matter is received under space and time, synthesised through categories, and pursued toward unity by reason.
core_sessions.consequence: The system secures empirical objectivity while replacing dogmatic metaphysics with a critique of reason's powers and limits.
core_sessions.trap: Do not say Kant privately creates objects, simply splits the difference between rationalism and empiricism, or owns ethics/aesthetics in this clause.
core_sessions.objection: If objects conform to our cognitive conditions, Kant may appear to secure only a world-for-us and not reality itself.
core_sessions.reply: Kant replies that knowledge requires conditions of possible experience, not a God's-eye comparison with things as they are independently of every knower.
core_sessions.limit: The reply secures empirical realism but leaves the status and affection of things in themselves contested.
core_sessions.exam: Use the architecture sensibility -> understanding -> reason, then evaluate the gain in objectivity against the noumenal limit.
revision: All cognition begins with experience, but not all arises from experience.
Transcendental asks for conditions of possible experience; transcendent exceeds experience.
Empirical realism and transcendental idealism are complementary, not contradictory.

core_sessions.title: Synthetic A Priori Judgments and the Copernican Revolution
core_sessions.plain: Kant's central puzzle is how a judgment can add knowledge yet be necessarily true before particular experience.
core_sessions.technical: A synthetic a priori judgment is ampliative because its predicate is not contained in its subject, yet necessary and universal because its warrant rests on a priori cognitive conditions rather than induction.
core_sessions.answer: Synthetic a priori judgments are possible because objects of possible experience must conform to the mind's a priori forms, so mathematics and fundamental natural principles articulate conditions under which anything can appear as an object for us.
core_sessions.usage: Define analytic and synthetic judgments, distinguish a priori from a posteriori warrant, identify the synthetic a priori class through mathematics and causality, explain the Copernican revolution, and end with its restriction to appearances.
core_sessions.mechanism: The knower supplies universal forms to sensory matter, making informative necessity possible for every object that can be experienced.
core_sessions.consequence: Mathematics and principles such as every event has a cause become objectively valid without becoming truths about things in themselves.
core_sessions.trap: Do not treat every a priori claim as analytic or present 7 + 5 = 12 as an empirical generalisation.
core_sessions.objection: Non-Euclidean geometry and modern physics weaken Kant's chosen scientific examples.
core_sessions.reply: Kant's deeper claim concerns enabling forms of experience; it need not stand or fall with every eighteenth-century example.
core_sessions.limit: The revised defence preserves the transcendental strategy but weakens claims of unrevisable content.
core_sessions.exam: For 'how possible' questions, use the regressive form: given objective knowledge, identify its necessary a priori conditions.
revision: Analytic concerns containment; synthetic concerns ampliation.
A priori concerns warrant independent of particular experience, not temporal innateness.
The revolution concerns objects of experience conforming to cognition.

visuals.title: Judgment matrix: analytic/synthetic x a priori/a posteriori
visuals.caption: The central class is informative and necessary at once.

| ANALYTIC       | predicate contained      | no genuine Kantian class  |

core_sessions.title: Space and Time: Pure Forms of Sensible Intuition
core_sessions.plain: Space and time are the unavoidable lenses through which sensory objects are given, not items discovered among those objects.
core_sessions.technical: In the Transcendental Aesthetic, space is the pure a priori form of outer sense and time the pure a priori form of inner sense and thereby of all representations; each is a singular intuition rather than a discursive concept.
core_sessions.answer: Space and time are a priori forms, transcendentally ideal yet empirically real; the 2019 wording must not be converted into transcendent space/time.
core_sessions.usage: Define form of intuition, distinguish outer and inner sense, reconstruct the a priori and intuitive arguments, then state empirical reality plus transcendental ideality.
core_sessions.mechanism: Space and time precede and organise sensory relations, allowing geometry, arithmetic, motion and ordered experience.
core_sessions.consequence: Kant rejects both their treatment as independent containers and their reduction to empirical abstractions.
core_sessions.trap: Do not call them innate images, empirical concepts, illusions or properties of things in themselves.
core_sessions.objection: Their subject-dependence appears to make experience merely subjective, while non-Euclidean geometry and relativity pressure Kant's scientific illustrations.
core_sessions.reply: The forms are intersubjective conditions of human experience, not private inventions; the historically informed defence separates the transcendental argument from the claim that physical geometry must be Euclidean.
core_sessions.limit: Kant does not independently prove that every possible rational sensibility must share our forms.
core_sessions.exam: For 15/20 marks, distinguish metaphysical exposition, transcendental exposition, and the two-sided verdict of ideality and reality.
revision: Space: outer sense; time: inner sense and all representations.
One space/time with parts within it indicates intuition, not a concept with instances.
Empty space/time can be represented; objects without them cannot be represented.

visuals.title: Space and time as forms of intuition
visuals.caption: The forms order what is given without describing things in themselves.
lines: SENSORY MATTER
+--> OUTER SENSE -> SPACE -> coexistence / geometry
+--> INNER SENSE -> TIME -> succession / arithmetic
-> every representation is temporal
EMPIRICALLY REAL: valid for every appearance
TRANSCENDENTALLY IDEAL: not predicates of things in themselves

visuals.title: Why space and time are a priori intuitions
visuals.caption: Kant combines priority arguments with singular-whole arguments.
lines: A PRIORI
1. outer/inner ordering presupposes space/time
2. objects may be removed; the forms cannot be removed
INTUITIVE, NOT CONCEPTUAL
3. one space and one time; regions/periods are limitations within them
4. infinite magnitude is represented as given, not built from instances

core_sessions.title: Categories, Synthesis and the Transcendental Unity of Apperception
core_sessions.plain: Categories are the understanding's a priori rules for combining the sensory manifold into one objective experience unified by transcendental apperception.
core_sessions.technical: Categories are twelve pure concepts of the understanding derived from functions of judgment; synthesis combines the manifold, while transcendental apperception is the formal unity expressed by the 'I think' that must be able to accompany every representation.
core_sessions.answer: The Transcendental Deduction justifies categories by showing that unified self-conscious experience is possible only through rule-governed synthesis, so the categories constitute objects of experience without depicting noumenal things.
core_sessions.usage: List all twelve categories in four triads, distinguish identification from justification, and reconstruct the manifold -> synthesis -> apperception -> object argument.
core_sessions.mechanism: The space-time manifold is objectively unified through categories because all representations must be combinable in one transcendental apperception.
core_sessions.consequence: Categories are necessary conditions of experience, not innate pictures copied onto independent reality.
core_sessions.trap: Do not infer a substantial soul from the 'I think' or apply the categories to noumena.
core_sessions.objection: The Deduction is notoriously difficult and may seem to infer objective validity from a requirement of self-consciousness.
core_sessions.reply: Kant's reply is that objectivity is not added after representations are unified; objective synthesis and apperceptive unity are two aspects of one rule-governed act.
core_sessions.limit: The argument secures categories for experience only if Kant's account of judgment and self-consciousness is exhaustive.
core_sessions.exam: For an exam answer, separate the metaphysical deduction, transcendental deduction, and limitation to possible experience.
revision: Intuitions without concepts are blind; concepts without intuitions are empty.
Apperception is a formal condition, not Hume's empirical bundle or Descartes' substance.
The Deduction answers quid juris: by what right do pure concepts apply?

core_sessions.title: Schematism: How Pure Categories Apply to Temporal Appearances
core_sessions.plain: A pure category and a sensory appearance are unlike, so Kant introduces a temporal rule that can connect them.
core_sessions.technical: A transcendental schema is a rule of productive imagination that determines time in a manner homogeneous with a category as an a priori rule and with appearances because every representation occurs in time; it is a procedure, not a mental image.
core_sessions.answer: Schematism converts logical functions into rules of temporal application, explaining how the Deduction's entitlement becomes usable for appearances while leaving unschematised categories without objective sense.
core_sessions.usage: State the heterogeneity problem, explain why time is the third thing, distinguish schema from image, and give the four time architectures.
core_sessions.mechanism: Time-series, time-content, time-order and time-scope mediate Quantity, Quality, Relation and Modality.
core_sessions.consequence: Pure categories acquire objective use only as schematised rules for appearances.
core_sessions.trap: Do not call a schema a picture resembling both a concept and an object.
core_sessions.objection: The bridge appears as obscure as the gap, and Kant calls schematism an art concealed in the depths of the human soul.
core_sessions.reply: The chapter's functional role is clear: without time-rules the Analogies and other Principles could not apply categories to experience.
core_sessions.limit: Functional necessity does not fully exhibit how productive imagination performs the mediation.
core_sessions.exam: Keep Core to rule, time and one example; reserve detailed A/B textual disputes for Advanced.
revision: Schema is a rule/procedure; image is a determinate product.
Number schematises Quantity; degree schematises Quality.
Relation becomes permanence, succession by rule and reciprocal coexistence.

visuals.title: The schematism bridge
visuals.caption: Time is the shared medium because every representation is temporal.
lines: PURE CATEGORY                 APPEARANCE
intellectual / universal      sensible / particular
v                v
TRANSCENDENTAL SCHEMA
rule of time-determination
category-side: a priori rule
intuition-side: every appearance is in time

visuals.title: Four time architectures
visuals.caption: The groups of categories become distinct modes of temporal determination.
lines: QUANTITY -> time-series -> NUMBER
QUALITY  -> time-content -> DEGREE / intensive magnitude
RELATION -> time-order -> permanence / succession / coexistence
MODALITY -> time-scope -> some time / determinate time / all times

core_sessions.title: Analogies of Experience: Substance, Causality and Community
core_sessions.plain: The Analogies of Experience are a priori principles that determine objective duration, succession and simultaneity through substance, causality and reciprocal community.
core_sessions.technical: The Analogies are principles that determine duration through permanence of substance, objective succession through causality, and simultaneity through reciprocal community; they constitute experience's temporal order without predicting particular empirical events.
core_sessions.answer: Kant answers Hume by arguing that causality is not inferred from repetition but presupposed in judging a succession as an objective event, though particular causal laws remain empirical.
core_sessions.usage: Define the three Analogies of Experience through permanence of substance, causal succession and reciprocal community; use the house/ship contrast to explain objective order and then qualify Kant's response to Hume.
core_sessions.mechanism: Persistent substance, irreversible succession under a rule, and reciprocal interaction act as proxies for duration, succession and simultaneity.
core_sessions.consequence: Experienced nature becomes a public temporal order rather than a private sequence of perceptions.
core_sessions.trap: Do not claim that Kant derives particular causal laws a priori or that every sequence of perceptions is an event.
core_sessions.objection: Strawson argues that an involuntary order of apprehension does not by itself establish natural causal necessity.
core_sessions.reply: The Kantian reply says objective temporal placement requires a rule stronger than subjective association, while empirical inquiry still discovers the particular cause.
core_sessions.limit: The reply establishes conceptual entitlement more securely than it proves any one law of nature.
core_sessions.exam: In Hume comparisons, locate the exact shift from observed conjunction to conditions of objective time-determination.
revision: First Analogy: substance persists through alteration.
Second Analogy: every event follows according to a causal rule.
Third Analogy: simultaneous substances stand in reciprocal community.

visuals.title: Three Analogies and the modes of time
visuals.caption: Each principle supplies a perceptible proxy for an unperceivable time-relation.
lines: TIME ITSELF CANNOT BE PERCEIVED
+--> DURATION -> permanence of SUBSTANCE
+--> SUCCESSION -> event ordered by CAUSAL RULE
+--> SIMULTANEITY -> reciprocal COMMUNITY

visuals.title: House and ship: subjective and objective succession
visuals.caption: The Second Analogy distinguishes chosen scanning from an event's fixed order.
lines: HOUSE
roof -> door or door -> roof | reversible apprehension
coexisting object; sequence belongs to my inspection
SHIP DOWNSTREAM
upstream -> downstream | irreversible objective succession
an event must be located through a rule: cause and effect

core_sessions.title: Phenomena, Noumena and Empirical Realism
core_sessions.plain: We know things only as they appear under our forms, while the notion of a thing apart from those forms marks a limit rather than a second object of science.
core_sessions.technical: A phenomenon is an object of possible experience structured by space, time and categories; a noumenon in the negative sense is a thing considered insofar as it is not an object of sensible intuition and functions as a limiting concept, not theoretical knowledge.
core_sessions.answer: Kant combines transcendental idealism with empirical realism: appearances are objective and public within experience, although categories cannot be extended to things in themselves.
core_sessions.usage: Define both sides, state the negative role of noumenon, explain empirical realism, and evaluate the two-world/two-aspect and affection tensions cautiously.
core_sessions.mechanism: Cognitive conditions establish the knowable phenomenal domain and simultaneously forbid constitutive claims beyond it.
core_sessions.consequence: Science is secured, Cartesian inner-world priority is challenged, and speculative metaphysics is bounded.
core_sessions.trap: Do not identify noumenon with a known hidden object: negative noumenon is a limit, positive noumenon requires intellectual intuition, and affection is disputed.
core_sessions.objection: Hegel asks how Kant can draw a boundary around what is unknowable, while Jacobi asks how unknown things can affect sensibility if causality applies only to appearances.
core_sessions.reply: Kant can treat noumenon negatively as a boundary concept and avoid claiming positive noumenal causation.
core_sessions.limit: The negative reading reduces contradiction but leaves the source of sensory matter under-described.
core_sessions.exam: Use 'two aspects' as a cautious interpretive option, not as uncontested Kantian doctrine.
revision: Phenomena are appearances, not deceptive seeming.
Noumenon is thinkable negatively but not knowable through theoretical reason.
The Refutation of Idealism proves empirically external objects, not noumenal objects.

science, causal law, public objects, empirical realism
THINKABLE LIMIT, NOT THEORETICAL KNOWLEDGE
NOUMENON / THING IN ITSELF in the negative sense

core_sessions.title: Ideas of Reason, Transcendental Illusion and the Paralogisms
core_sessions.plain: Understanding organises experience, whereas reason asks for a complete, unconditioned ground that experience can never present as an object.
core_sessions.technical: Ideas of soul, world and God regulate systematic unity; the ens realissimum is the Ideal of complete determination until speculative theology hypostatizes it.
core_sessions.answer: Transcendental illusion is natural and persistent because reason cannot stop seeking completion, yet critique can prevent the slide from useful systematic unity to metaphysical claims about soul-substance, world-totality and God.
core_sessions.usage: Distinguish understanding from reason, map soul/world/God, define both uses, explain persistent illusion, and use the Paralogisms to show the soul error.
core_sessions.mechanism: Reason projects complete explanatory unity and then mistakes a methodological ideal for a constitutively given object.
core_sessions.consequence: The Ideas organise inquiry fruitfully but generate paralogisms, antinomies and failed theology when reified.
core_sessions.trap: Do not say the Ideas are categories, empirical hypotheses or useless fictions.
core_sessions.objection: If regulative Ideas have no object known to correspond to them, their systematic authority may appear merely heuristic.
core_sessions.reply: Kant replies that reason's demand for unity is a necessary norm of inquiry even though it cannot certify transcendent objects.
core_sessions.limit: The norm guides discovery but cannot independently prove that nature forms one complete rational system.
core_sessions.exam: Use the soul's Paralogisms briefly unless the question directly asks rational psychology.
revision: Understanding supplies rules to appearances; reason seeks principles and completion.
Regulative means guide inquiry; constitutive means determine an object.
The logical 'I think' cannot be converted into a simple immortal soul.

visuals.title: Soul, world and God as Ideas of Reason
visuals.caption: Each Idea projects an unconditioned totality that cannot be given in experience.
lines: REASON SEEKS THE UNCONDITIONED
+--> SOUL -> complete unity of inner conditions
|             danger: 'I think' -> soul-substance
+--> WORLD -> complete series of cosmological conditions
|             danger: antinomies
+--> GOD -> complete ground of all conditions
danger: speculative proofs

visuals.title: Regulative and constitutive uses
visuals.caption: The same Idea can guide inquiry legitimately or generate illusion when reified.
lines: REGULATIVE USE
'Investigate AS IF nature formed maximal systematic unity'
guide / heuristic / orientation -> legitimate
CONSTITUTIVE USE
'Soul, world-totality or God is known as an object'
object-claim beyond intuition -> transcendental illusion

core_sessions.title: The Four Antinomies and the Different Forms of Their Resolution
core_sessions.plain: Kant's four antinomies are thesis-antithesis conflicts generated when reason treats the complete world-series as a finished object beyond possible experience.
core_sessions.technical: An antinomy is a thesis-antithesis pair for which pure reason constructs apparently valid proofs after extending cosmological principles beyond possible experience; the first two are mathematical and the last two dynamical.
core_sessions.answer: Transcendental idealism resolves the mathematical antinomies by rejecting the shared assumption of a given world-whole, while it reconciles the dynamical antinomies by distinguishing phenomenal natural conditions from a merely intelligible standpoint.
core_sessions.usage: Define antinomy, state all four thesis-antithesis pairs, distinguish mathematical from dynamical antinomies, explain their different resolutions, and evaluate the room secured for freedom without claiming knowledge of noumena.
core_sessions.mechanism: Antinomy arises when reason treats the unconditioned world-series as a completed object in itself and attempts opposed transcendental proofs.
core_sessions.consequence: The antinomies expose speculative metaphysics' limit and make freedom compatible with phenomenal natural causality at an intelligible boundary.
core_sessions.trap: Do not flatten all four into 'both false' or 'both true', and do not treat the fourth antinomy as a proof of God.
core_sessions.objection: The resolution may look like avoiding contradiction by assigning opposed claims to an unknowable domain.
core_sessions.reply: Kant answers that the contradiction arose from transcendental realism; once appearances are not things in themselves, the shared premise dissolves or the standpoints separate.
core_sessions.limit: The dynamical resolution makes freedom thinkable rather than theoretically known, leaving its positive content to practical philosophy.
core_sessions.exam: A 20-marker must spend more space on construction and resolution than on listing the pairs.
revision: First: world beginning/limits versus no beginning/limits.
Second: simple parts versus no simple parts.
Third: freedom plus nature versus universal natural causality.
Fourth: necessary being versus no necessary being.

visuals.title: Antinomy 1: magnitude of the world
visuals.caption: Both sides assume the world-series is a completed object.
lines: THESIS: The world has a beginning in time and limits in space.
ANTITHESIS: The world has no beginning or spatial limits; it is infinite.
RESOLUTION: the world-whole is not given as finite or completed infinite.

visuals.title: Antinomy 2: composition of the world
visuals.caption: The dispute illegitimately treats appearances as a completed totality of parts.
lines: THESIS: Every composite consists ultimately of simple parts.
ANTITHESIS: Nothing simple exists; every composite is further divisible.
RESOLUTION: neither predicate describes a world-whole given in experience.

visuals.title: Antinomy 3: freedom and natural causality
visuals.caption: The dynamical opposition can be separated by standpoint.
lines: THESIS: Causality through freedom is required besides natural causality.
ANTITHESIS: There is no freedom; every event occurs by laws of nature.
RESOLUTION: natural determination for appearances; intelligible freedom is thinkable.

visuals.title: Antinomy 4: necessary being
visuals.caption: The resolution permits a thought-limit but supplies no theoretical proof.
lines: THESIS: An absolutely necessary being belongs to the world as part or cause.
ANTITHESIS: No absolutely necessary being exists in or beyond the world.
RESOLUTION: empirical contingency remains; a noumenal ground is merely thinkable.

visuals.title: Why the two resolutions differ
visuals.caption: Mathematical totalisation fails; dynamical predicates can be standpoint-qualified.
lines: ANTINOMIES 1-2: MATHEMATICAL
same false presupposition -> no given finite/infinite or simple/composite whole
ANTINOMIES 3-4: DYNAMICAL
phenomenal conditions remain valid
intelligible freedom/ground is possible but not theoretically known

core_sessions.title: Critique of the Three Proofs for God and the Final Critical Balance
core_sessions.plain: Kant does not prove atheism; he argues that theoretical reason cannot demonstrate God by turning a concept, causal series or observed order into a necessary creator.
core_sessions.technical: The ontological proof fails because existence is not a real predicate adding content to a concept; the cosmological proof illicitly extends causal reasoning beyond experience and depends on the ontological identification of necessary being with the ens realissimum; the design proof reaches at most an architect and borrows the other proofs to reach a necessary creator.
core_sessions.answer: Kant's critique removes God from theoretical knowledge rather than from thought or practical faith, completing a system that secures phenomenal objectivity precisely by refusing constitutive claims beyond possible experience.
keywords: existence is not a real predicate
core_sessions.usage: Treat each proof as argument -> Kantian objection -> residual value, then distinguish theoretical agnosticism from atheism and conclude with the critical balance.
core_sessions.mechanism: All three routes attempt to turn thought beyond experience into constitutive knowledge, and the latter two ultimately require the ontological step.
core_sessions.consequence: Speculative God-proofs fail; lawful phenomenal Nature is constituted through understanding, while Hegel contests Kant's fixed dualisms and unknowable remainder.
core_sessions.trap: Do not say Kant disproves God's existence or let the practical postulate become a Paper II detour.
core_sessions.objection: Modal ontological arguments dispute whether necessary existence can be analysed as an ordinary predicate, while design may retain probabilistic force.
core_sessions.reply: Kant's objection decisively blocks the classical concept-to-existence inference and correctly limits what finite order can establish.
core_sessions.limit: The critique is strongest against demonstration and weaker against non-demonstrative religious inference.
core_sessions.exam: For 'critically examine', reconstruct the classical proof accurately before presenting Kant, an objection, reply and graded verdict.
revision: Existence posits an object; it does not enlarge its concept.
Cosmological reasoning both overextends causality and covertly returns to ontology.
Design suggests order at most; it cannot establish an infinite necessary creator.

visuals.title: Ontological proof: concept cannot yield actuality
visuals.caption: Kant blocks the inference at the claim that existence is a perfection.
lines: PROOF: God = most perfect being -> existence is perfection -> God exists
KANT: existence is not a content-adding real predicate
100 possible thalers and 100 actual thalers have the same concept
RESIDUAL: a concept may be coherent without being instantiated

visuals.title: Cosmological proof: causal overreach plus hidden ontology
visuals.caption: The proof cannot identify a necessary ground as God without the failed first proof.
lines: PROOF: contingent existence -> necessary ground -> God
KANT 1: causality is valid only within possible experience
KANT 2: necessary being = ens realissimum repeats ontological reasoning
RESIDUAL: contingency can motivate inquiry, not theoretical demonstration

visuals.title: Physico-theological proof: architect, not necessary creator
visuals.caption: Observed order cannot carry the conclusion assigned to it.
lines: PROOF: purposive order -> intelligent designer -> creator God
KANT: order supports at most a powerful architect of given material
to reach creator/necessity it borrows cosmological and ontological steps
RESIDUAL: limited analogical or heuristic force, not apodictic proof

visuals.title: Critical balance and comparison
visuals.caption: Kant's gain and cost can be stated on matched axes.
lines: RATIONALISM: a priori necessity, but transcendent dogma
EMPIRICISM: sensory content, but necessity reduced to habit
KANT: a priori conditions + sensory matter -> phenomenal objectivity
GAIN: mathematics/science and empirical realism
LIMIT: no theoretical knowledge of soul, world-whole or God
TENSION: unknowable noumenon and the affection problem

ascii_panels.title: Critical starting problem and the rationalism-empiricism synthesis
lines: CENTRAL QUESTION: How can cognition be informative, necessary and objectively valid?
RATIONALISM -> a priori necessity, but dogmatic claims about soul, world and God
EMPIRICISM / HUME -> sensory content, but no experienced necessary connection
KANTIAN CRITIQUE -> sensory matter + a priori form, restricted to possible experience
COPERNICAN REVOLUTION -> objects AS EXPERIENCED conform to cognitive conditions
SENSIBILITY -> intuitions in space/time -> UNDERSTANDING -> categories and objects
UNDERSTANDING -> REASON -> Ideas of Soul, World and God; drive to the unconditioned
TRANSCENDENTAL = conditions of possible experience; TRANSCENDENT = beyond experience
RESULT -> empirical realism + transcendental idealism + limit on theoretical reason
ANSWER LINE -> Kant secures objectivity by making its a priori conditions mind-given.

ascii_panels.title: Synthetic a priori judgments and the Copernican explanation
lines: ANALYTIC -> predicate contained in subject; denial contradicts the concept
SYNTHETIC -> predicate adds content; denial is not self-contradictory
A PRIORI -> necessary/universal warrant independent of particular experience
A POSTERIORI -> empirical, informative and contingent warrant
ANALYTIC A PRIORI -> 'Bodies are extended'; ANALYTIC A POSTERIORI -> no Kantian class
SYNTHETIC A POSTERIORI -> 'This table is brown'; informative but contingent
SYNTHETIC A PRIORI -> 7 + 5 = 12; every event has a cause; informative + necessary
HOW POSSIBLE? -> the mind supplies space, time and categories to every appearance
MATHEMATICS / FUNDAMENTAL SCIENCE -> valid for objects of possible experience
LIMIT -> no inference from these forms to things in themselves or transcendent objects

ascii_panels.title: Transcendental Aesthetic: space and time as forms of intuition
lines: FORM OF INTUITION -> a priori way in which sensory matter can be given
SPACE -> pure form of OUTER sense; coexistence, externality and geometry
TIME -> pure form of INNER sense; succession and all representations
A PRIORI ARGUMENT -> spatial/temporal ordering presupposes, not produces, the forms
NECESSITY ARGUMENT -> empty space/time is representable; objects without them are not
INTUITION ARGUMENT -> one space/time; regions and periods are limitations within it
INFINITY ARGUMENT -> magnitude is represented as a given whole, not instances under a concept
EMPIRICALLY REAL -> objectively valid for every appearance and possible experience
TRANSCENDENTALLY IDEAL -> not properties of things in themselves
OBJECTION -> modern geometry/science pressures examples, not the whole transcendental strategy

ascii_panels.title: Categories, synthesis and transcendental unity of apperception
lines: QUANTITY -> Unity | Plurality | Totality
QUALITY -> Reality | Negation | Limitation
RELATION -> Inherence/Subsistence | Causality/Dependence | Community/Reciprocity
MODALITY -> Possibility/Impossibility | Existence/Non-existence | Necessity/Contingency
METAPHYSICAL DEDUCTION -> identifies categories from functions of judgment
TRANSCENDENTAL DEDUCTION -> justifies their objective application
MANIFOLD -> SYNTHESIS under rules -> 'I THINK' can accompany each representation
APPERCEPTION -> formal unity of self-consciousness, not empirical ego or soul-substance
OBJECTIVE UNITY -> the same rule unites representations as one experience of objects
LIMIT -> categories constitute appearances only; they do not picture or determine noumena

ascii_panels.title: Schematism: temporal bridge from pure category to appearance
lines: PROBLEM -> pure intellectual category and sensible particular appearance are heterogeneous
SCHEMA -> rule/procedure of productive imagination; never a determinate mental image
WHY TIME? -> it is a priori like the category and contains every representation
QUANTITY / time-series -> NUMBER through successive homogeneous addition
QUALITY / time-content -> DEGREE or intensive magnitude
RELATION / time-order -> permanence, succession by rule, reciprocal coexistence
MODALITY / time-scope -> some time, determinate time, all times
DEDUCTION proves THAT categories apply; SCHEMATISM explains HOW they apply
UNSCHEMATISED CATEGORY -> logical function without objective sense for appearances
RESIDUAL -> Kant calls the mediating operation an art concealed in the human soul

ascii_panels.title: Analogies of Experience and Kant's precise answer to Hume
lines: MASTER PREMISE -> time itself cannot be perceived; objective time needs proxies
FIRST ANALOGY / duration -> substance persists while its states alter
SECOND ANALOGY / succession -> every event follows according to a causal rule
THIRD ANALOGY / simultaneity -> substances coexist through reciprocal community
HOUSE -> viewing order is reversible; succession belongs to my apprehension
SHIP DOWNSTREAM -> order is irreversible; an objective event requires a rule
ANTI-HUME MOVE -> causality is a condition of judging objective succession, not habit
QUALIFICATION -> particular causal laws remain empirical and require investigation
STRAWSON OBJECTION -> involuntary order does not automatically prove natural necessity
VERDICT -> Kant secures entitlement to causality more clearly than any particular law

ascii_panels.title: Phenomena, noumena, empirical realism and the idealism boundary
lines: PHENOMENON -> object as given in space/time and thought through categories
POSSIBLE EXPERIENCE -> knowable, public, causal and scientifically investigable domain
NOUMENON NEGATIVELY -> thing considered apart from sensible intuition; limiting concept
NOUMENON IS THINKABLE, NOT KNOWABLE -> no theoretical predicates from the categories
TRANSCENDENTAL IDEALISM -> our forms condition appearances
EMPIRICAL REALISM -> external objects are real within experience, not private illusions
REFUTATION -> determinate inner time-awareness requires an empirically external permanent
TWO-ASPECT READING -> one object considered as appearance and independently of our access
HEGEL/JACOBI PRESSURE -> boundary knowledge and affection threaten internal consistency
SAFE VERDICT -> negative limitation is defensible; positive noumenal causation is not

ascii_panels.title: Ideas of Reason, regulative unity and natural transcendental illusion
lines: UNDERSTANDING -> supplies rules for appearances; REASON -> seeks the unconditioned
SOUL -> projected complete unity of inner conditions
WORLD -> projected complete totality of cosmological conditions
GOD -> projected complete ground of all conditions and reality
REGULATIVE USE -> guide inquiry toward systematic unity; legitimate 'as if'
CONSTITUTIVE USE -> claim the Idea determines a known object; illegitimate
TRANSCENDENTAL ILLUSION -> natural and persistent drive to reify completion
PARALOGISM -> logical 'I think' is misread as simple, substantial, enduring soul
VALUE -> systematic research and explanatory integration
DANGER -> paralogisms, antinomies and speculative theology

ascii_panels.title: Four cosmological antinomies and their differentiated resolutions
lines: 1 THESIS -> beginning in time + spatial limit | ANTITHESIS -> infinite time/space
2 THESIS -> composites end in simple parts | ANTITHESIS -> nothing simple exists
3 THESIS -> freedom besides nature | ANTITHESIS -> universal natural causality
4 THESIS -> absolutely necessary being | ANTITHESIS -> no necessary being
SOURCE OF CONFLICT -> categories applied to the world-series as a completed whole
MATHEMATICAL 1-2 -> reject shared assumption that a finite/infinite whole is given
DYNAMICAL 3-4 -> phenomenal conditions and intelligible standpoint can be distinguished
FREEDOM -> thinkable noumenally while every appearance remains naturally determined
NECESSARY GROUND -> thinkable boundary, not theoretical proof of God
SIGNIFICANCE -> indirect case for idealism and limit of speculative metaphysics

ascii_panels.title: God-proof critique, evaluation ledger, traps, PYQs and answer spine
lines: ONTOLOGICAL -> perfect concept includes existence | KANT -> existence adds no content
100 possible/actual thalers -> same concept; actuality cannot be extracted analytically
COSMOLOGICAL -> contingent exists, therefore necessary God | illicit causal extension
COSMOLOGICAL DEPENDENCE -> necessary being = ens realissimum repeats ontological proof
DESIGN -> order implies designer | at most an architect, not necessary creator
DESIGN DEPENDENCE -> creator/necessity needs cosmological then ontological steps
BOUNDARY -> theoretical proof fails; this is not a demonstration of atheism
COMPARISON -> rationalist necessity + empiricist content under critical limitation
PYQ ROUTES -> synthesis, space/time, apperception, antinomies, Hume and God proofs
ANSWER SPINE -> thesis -> doctrine -> argument -> objection/reply -> qualified verdict
FINAL VERDICT -> Kant gains phenomenal objectivity at the cost of noumenal agnosticism
